title: The Royal Rivalry, Episode 1: Who Is the Greatest? (full episode)
series: The Royal Rivalry (Clash of Clans fan comic), full episodes

lines: Every legend begins somewhere. Ours begins in the dark, with a pair of eyes that should not be there.
But to understand what those eyes were watching, we have to go back. Back to an argument.
In a green valley, ringed by mighty walls, there stood a kingdom of builders, soldiers and dreamers.
Its towers were tall. Its gold was plentiful. And its people were, mostly, happy.
And the Wizards, well, the Wizards mostly set things on fire by accident.
Leading them all were two heroes. The first was the Barbarian King.
Loud, brave, and always the first to charge, usually before anyone had finished making a plan.
Plans are for people who can't punch!
The second was the Archer Queen.
Calm, precise, and she had never missed a shot in her life. Or so she liked to remind everyone.
Eleven thousand bullseyes. But who's counting? Me. I am counting.
Together, they kept the kingdom safe from every threat.
They kept the peace with everyone. Except each other.
Morning. You have breakfast in your beard.
Nobody remembers exactly when the two heroes first arrived. Mostly because they arrived on the very same day, at the very same gate, at the very same moment.
By half a step. Which you tripped over.
They have been arguing about that half a step ever since.
The Grand Warden remembered it well. Back then, the kingdom was just a few huts and a wall made of fence posts.
They were the bravest heroes I had ever seen. And the loudest. By far the loudest.
Together, they had turned that little camp into a kingdom. Not that either of them would ever admit the other one had helped.
Every morning, the King trained his Barbarians in the town square.
Again! Swing like you mean it! Faster! LOUDER!
The Barbarians swung. They yelled. One of them fell over.
Across the square, the Queen trained her Archers in perfect silence.
Twenty arrows. Twenty bullseyes. Then she turned, slowly enough to make sure the King was watching.
Arrows! A real hero fights up close, where the danger is!
A real hero fights where she won't get her crown dented.
My crown has NEVER been dented.
His crown had been dented eleven times.
At lunch, the royal feast was served. Power pancakes. Hero skewers. And a cake shaped like the Clan Castle.
There was exactly one pancake left.
That pancake is mine. I trained all morning.
I hit twenty bullseyes. Before breakfast.
They reached for it at the very same time.
I'll, uh, go get a mop.
That afternoon, the town council met to discuss something important: the kingdom's brand new statue.
The council proposes a statue of the kingdom's greatest hero, right here in the square.
Ah. I was worried this would happen.

caps.text: I was worried this would happen.

lines: Within minutes, the whole village had chosen sides.
Soon, the village was placing bets.
Fifty on them both falling into the fountain.
The Wizard was about to win a lot of gold.
Nobody noticed the small green visitor slipping through the crowd.
Ooh, shiny. And shiny. And very, very shiny.
Has anyone seen my coin purse?
I have charged into a hundred battles!
And I won them for you, from the back.
I could beat you with one hand!
You'd need the other one to find your sword.
The argument became a challenge. The challenge became a duel, right in the middle of the square.
The King charged. The Queen stepped aside. And the King, unable to stop, sailed straight into the fountain.
The Queen laughed so hard she slipped, and followed him in.
The Healer, who had seen all of this before, sighed and patched them both up.
Again? This is the fourth time this week.
Then the ground shook. Just a little. The way it does when a very old, very tired wizard has heard enough.
A hero is not measured by how loud they shout, or how many arrows they count.
A hero is measured by what they do when the kingdom needs them.
The King and Queen nodded wisely. Then went straight back to glaring at each other.
Very well. A contest. The next time goblins raid this kingdom, whoever stops them, alone, will be named its greatest hero.
And the statue, of course, would be theirs.
They shook hands. It lasted eleven seconds, and both of them squeezed the entire time.
Later that evening, the Warden found the King alone in the training yard.
You charge into everything, my friend. One day, you will charge into something you cannot punch.
The Warden sighed. It was a very long sigh.
Then he found the Queen, on the archery range, still practicing by moonlight.
You never miss. But you never let anyone stand beside you, either.
People beside me get in the way of my shots.
The King sharpened his sword, until it was sharp enough to slice through a rumor.
The Queen restrung her crossbow forty times. Just to be sure.
On the last day, both heroes secretly visited the gold storage, to study where the goblins might strike.
Each one hid behind a barrel the moment the other walked in.
I can see your entire body.
Then came the night watch. The King on the east wall. The Queen on the west.
Each pretending not to check whether the other was still awake.
Meanwhile, in a muddy camp beyond the walls, lived the Goblin Boss.
He had raided this kingdom forty times. He had lost thirty-nine of them. But he was an optimist.
Forty-one is my lucky number. I can feel it.
Listen up! Tonight, we hit the gold storage.
What about the King and Queen?
Rule one: don't wake the King. Rule two: definitely don't annoy the Queen.
Rule three. What was rule three?
Just after midnight, twenty small green shadows crept toward the wall.
On the wall, a single Barbarian stood guard. He had been awake for nineteen hours.
They slipped through a crack in the wall, straight into the gold storage.
Both heroes heard the alarm. Both leapt from the walls. Both ran for the very same door.
The Queen fired an arrow to slow the goblins down.
It slowed down the King instead, pinning his cape to a barrel.
Fill every pocket! Fill every hat!
Boss, I've run out of pockets.
Inside, it was chaos. Gold coins flew everywhere.
Goblins stuffed their pockets, their hats, and, as instructed, their ears.
Then the King and Queen both spotted the same tiny goblin. And both charged.
They met in the middle. Hard.
Thanks for the gold! Same time next week?
By dawn, the gold storage was nearly empty.
Two heroes. Twenty goblins. And not a single one caught.
The villagers gathered around the empty storage, very quietly.
So, who pays out my bet now?
Technically, they both fell in the fountain. I win.
Neither of you won this contest. The kingdom lost it.
In the town square, the statue's stone stood uncarved. Waiting for a hero who had not yet earned it.
The King walked past it twice. The Queen walked past it three times. Neither of them said a word.
And for the first time, each of them wondered if the other might be, just a little bit, right.
Nice shot, earlier. On the cape.
From his tower, the Grand Warden watched them both.
Two halves of one hero. If only they knew it.
Then a cold wind blew across the valley, and the Warden frowned. He knew that wind. It smelled of lightning.
But far beyond the walls, on top of a storm-dark hill, something had watched the whole thing.
To be continued. Who is the greatest hero, the King or the Queen? Tell me in the comments.
